affiliation: ML PhD Student, UC Berkeley (Center for Human-Compatible AI)
title: Interpreting Personalized Reward Model Bases
blurb: RLHF-based alignment assumes a single stakeholder perspective, but in practice reward models are trained on feedback from diverse individuals with different values. A family of methods addresses this by learning a small set of reward "bases", where each person's preferences are expressed as a linear combination of those bases. The safety problem: no existing work actually interprets what these bases represent. Without interpretability, the bases cannot be used for monitoring or control.

affiliation: Principal Consultant, Nyaya Labs; Founder, The Surrogate Science Project
title: Interpretability for Scientific Causal Reasoning
blurb: How do we know whether the reasoning process by which a model arrives at an answer is actually trustworthy? Current LLM evaluations lack causal reasoning problems representative of real world science. Building on a prior benchmark on causal reasoning in drug toxicity evaluation, fellows will apply and evaluate interpretability tools on scientific reasoning problems.

affiliation: Lecturer on AI Safety; Founder, CCI
title: Do Rules and Concepts Hold Across Languages?
blurb: AI safety and compliance rules are almost exclusively written in English, but the models being deployed operate across many languages. This project investigates: when a rule is embedded into a model's internal representation space in one language, does it hold in another? And when it degrades, how and why?

title: Preference Drift in Language Models
theme: How preferences move across SFT, DPO and GRPO
blurb: As a model is trained on certain capabilities, do its preferences over which tasks it wants to do shift in ways it cannot anticipate? If a model trained heavily on coding begins to "want" coding tasks more than before, that has direct implications for how cohesive an agent the model is becoming, which is itself a safety-relevant signal.

title: Multilingual Safety Evals
blurb: AI safety evaluations are almost exclusively conducted in English. Yet models are increasingly deployed in high-stakes government services across multilingual populations. Do safety properties hold when the same models are tested in other languages? Do safety and capability claims in frontier model system cards generalize?

affiliation: Senior Lecturer in Computing and Data Science, University of Greenwich
title: Decision Update Consistency in LLMs
blurb: This project investigates how large language models update decisions when confronted with conflicting evidence. We introduce the concept of Decision Update Consistency (DUC) to assess whether models appropriately revise, resist, or over-weight prior recommendations when new information is introduced.

title: How AI Labs Redefine Safety
theme: Close-coding the labs' own safety documents
blurb: When frontier AI labs launch new models, do their safety standards stay consistent or do the definitions of safety, risk, and frontier itself quietly shift? This project investigates how major AI labs have changed their safety definitions, benchmarking practices, and model documentation over time.

title: Estimating Harm and Exposure for AI Harm Monitoring
blurb: A methodology is being developed to track specific AI harms over time, by estimating both harm counts and exposure to harm. With both, we can determine whether a harm is mitigating, escalating, receding, or concentrating. This project explores ways to automate this classification.

affiliation: Associate Professor, University of Wollongong in Dubai
title: Trust Calibration in Healthcare AI
blurb: This project explores how AI output design influences user trust and decision-making in AI-assisted healthcare contexts. A key AI safety concern is overreliance on AI systems when users interpret confident outputs as reliable without sufficient scrutiny.

title: Synchronous Monitoring for AI Control
blurb: Current AI control research focuses largely on detecting attacks after the fact. This project addresses an open question: can monitors reliably detect and respond to attacks while they are happening? Extending prior async control work to the synchronous setting has direct implications for deploying AI safely in real-time, high-stakes environments.

affiliation: Senior Scientist, Potsdam Inst. for Climate Impact Research / Zuse Inst. Berlin
title: Grounding Safe-by-Design AI
theme: From verbal situations to formal world models
blurb: Safe-by-design AI frameworks require agents to have a formal, tractable model of the world. This project tests how well LLMs can construct hierarchies of stochastic games encoded in JSON, representing the safety-relevant states, actions, and consequences of situations where an AI agent interacts with human and/or AI agents.

title: Red-Teaming Protein Foundation Models
blurb: Protein foundation models are widely deployed in drug discovery and synthetic biology, but adversarial robustness evaluations remain limited. This team will extend adversarial evaluation to ESM2 and introduce more biologically grounded metrics. Responsible disclosure is built into the timeline.
